arxiv-2108-01524.title: Generalising Kapranov’s Theorem For Tropical Geometry over Hyperfields
arxiv-2108-01524.creator: James Maxwell
arxiv-2108-01524.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by James Maxwell. Kapranov’s theorem is a foundational result in tropical geometry. It states that the set of tropicalisations of points on a hypersurface coincides precisely with the tropical variety of the tropicalisation of the defining polynomial. The aim of this paper is to generalise Kapranov’s theorem, replacing the role of a valuation, 𝑡𝑟𝑜𝑝 : K → ℝ ∪ { − ∞ } \mathit{trop}:K\rightarrow\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\} , with a more general class of hyperfield homomorphisms, ℍ → 𝕋 \mathbb{H}\rightarrow\mathbb{T} , which satisfy a relative algebraic closure condition.

arxiv-2108-02587.title: Four-Valued Semantics for Deductive Databases
arxiv-2108-02587.creator: Dominique Laurent, Nicolas Spyratos
arxiv-2108-02587.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Dominique Laurent, Nicolas Spyratos. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach to deductive databases meant to take into account the needs of current applications in the area of data integration. To this end, we extend the formalism of standard deductive databases to the context of Four-valued logic so as to account for unknown , inconsistent , true or false information under the open world assumption.

arxiv-2204-03424.title: Low complexity joint position and channel estimation at millimeter wave based on multidimensional orthogonal matching pursuit
arxiv-2204-03424.creator: Joan Palacios, Nuria González-Prelcic, Cristian Rusu
arxiv-2204-03424.description: Abstract Compressive approaches provide a means of effective channel high resolution channel estimates in millimeter wave MIMO systems, despite the use of analog and hybrid architectures. Such estimates can also be used as part of a joint channel estimation and localization solution. Achieving good localization performance, though, requires high resolution channel estimates and better methods to exploit those channels.

arxiv-2206-06519.creator: Andrew Eberhardt, Michael Kopp, Tom Abel
arxiv-2206-06519.description: Abstract We investigate the timescale on which quantum corrections alter the predictions of classical field theory for scalar field dark matter. This is accomplished by including second order terms in the evolution proportional to the covariance of the field operators.

arxiv-2211-04513.title: Bit models of replica wormholes
arxiv-2211-04513.creator: Henry Maxfield
arxiv-2211-04513.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Henry Maxfield. We define bit models of evaporating black holes which incorporate the effects of replica wormholes. These enter as non-perturbative corrections to the gravitational inner product, arising from spacetime wormholes that connect replica black holes. The resulting models have exactly unitary evolution, predict measurements on Hawking radiation in accord with a Page curve for entropy, and are compatible with a smooth horizon for infalling observers.

arxiv-2305-01655.title: Predicting blood pressure under circumstances of missing data: An analysis of missing data patterns and imputation methods using NHANES
arxiv-2305-01655.creator: Harish Chauhan, Nikunj Gupta, Zoe Haskell-Craig
arxiv-2305-01655.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Harish Chauhan, Nikunj Gupta, Zoe Haskell-Craig. * * footnotetext: These authors contributed equally to this work. Motivation The World Health Organization defines cardio-vascular disease (CVD) as “a group of disorders of the heart and blood vessels,” including coronary heart disease and stroke. ( World Health Organization 2021 ) CVD is affected by “intermediate risk factors” such as raised blood pressure, raised blood glucose, raised blood lipids, and obesity.

arxiv-2509-14989.title: UCorr: Wire Detection and Depth Estimation for Autonomous Drones
arxiv-2509-14989.creator: Benedikt Kolbeinsson and Krystian Mikolajczyk Imperial College London bk915@imperial.ac.uk, k.mikolajczyk@imperial.ac.uk
arxiv-2509-14989.description: Abstract In the realm of fully autonomous drones, the accurate detection of obstacles is paramount to ensure safe navigation and prevent collisions. Among these challenges, the detection of wires stands out due to their slender profile, which poses a unique and intricate problem.

arxiv-2602-05334.title: NeuCLIRTech: Chinese Monolingual and Cross-Language Information Retrieval Evaluation in a Challenging Domain
arxiv-2602-05334.creator: Dawn Lawrie, James Mayfield, Eugene Yang, Andrew Yates, Sean MacAvaney, Ronak Pradeep, Scott Miller, Paul McNamee, Luca Soldaini
arxiv-2602-05334.description: Abstract Measuring advances in retrieval requires test collections with relevance judgments that can faithfully distinguish systems. This paper presents NeuCLIRTech, an evaluation collection for cross-language retrieval over technical information. The collection consists of technical documents written natively in Chinese and those same documents machine translated into English. It includes 110 queries with relevance judgments.

pmc-11653204.description: Epidermal growth factor receptors (EGFRs) regulate the growth and repair process of epithelia, as well as carcinogenesis. However, whether EGFR signalling is responsible for skin inflammation remains elusive.

pmc-12521041.title: Methodological and Contextual Considerations in Assessing Internet Addiction and Eating Disorder Risk Among Bangladeshi Adolescents

pmc-12521041.description: BackgroundInternet addiction and eating disorders are emerging public health concerns among adolescents, particularly in South Asia. pmc-12542374.title: Exploring the role of miR-126 in diabetes and its complications: a comprehensive review
pmc-12542374.creator: Yousef Rasmi, Masoumeh Farahani, Elmira Roshani Asl, Shirin Barati, Nima Naseri, Kakali Ghoshal
pmc-12542374.description: Diabetes is a metabolic disorder primarily characterized by hyperglycemia, posing a substantial global health concern. Insulin resistance significantly contributes to the pathogenesis of type 2 diabetes and its associated complications, such as cardiovascular diseases and dyslipidemia. MicroRNAs (miRNAs), critical regulators of gene expression, have emerged as essential mediators in diabetes and its related pathological conditions.

pmc-12682520.title: Kupffer phase echo level ratio in contrast-enhanced ultrasound for differentiating malignant liver tumors
pmc-12682520.creator: Zheyuan Zhang, Qingting Tan, Xiuming Wang, Xia Xie, Lei Zhang, Huabin Zhang, Zhiyong Bai
pmc-12682520.description: BackgroundKupffer phase contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) using Sonazoid allows real-time assessment of Kupffer cell function, which is often disrupted in malignant liver tumors. While qualitative assessment is established, quantitative studies remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic value of the echo level ratio (ELR) derived from the Kupffer phase for differentiating hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) from non-HCC liver malignancies.

pmc-12699201.title: Comparative Evaluation of Centrifugation Speed and Its Impact on Diagnostic Accuracy
pmc-12699201.creator: Mohammed A Jeraiby, Jobran M Moshi, Sajad A Dar, Mahmoud M Habibullah, Mjery Yahia, Saif Elden B Abdalla, Raheem M Balkhtab, Renad A Saigh, Nahlah S burayk
pmc-12699201.description: IntroductionTimely laboratory results are essential for effective clinical decision‐making, with turnaround time (TAT) serving as a key performance indicator. Pre‐analytical steps like centrifugation significantly impact TAT. This study investigates whether a shorter, high‐speed centrifugation can reduce TAT while maintaining the analytical accuracy required for routine diagnostic testing.MethodologyThis comparative experimental study analyzed blood samples from patients using plasma and serum tubes.
